## Valuation Insights

Costco’s fiscal year 2026 revenue reached $303.154 billion, representing a 10.1% increase from the prior year’s $275.235 billion. This growth reflects steady expansion across its membership base and global footprint.
<!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax|period=2025-09-01/2026-08-30|value=303154000000] -->

<!-- [source: ratio|operation=divide|inputs=303154000000;275235000000|result=10.14%|definition=Revenue growth = (Current Revenue - Prior Revenue) / Prior Revenue] -->

The company generated $11.685 billion in operating income on that revenue, yielding an operating margin of approximately 3.85%. This margin is calculated as operating income divided by total revenue and indicates the profitability of core operations before interest and taxes.
<!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss|period=2025-09-01/2026-08-30|value=11685000000] -->
<!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax|period=2025-09-01/2026-08-30|value=303154000000] -->
<!-- [source: ratio|operation=divide|inputs=11685000000;303154000000|result=3.85%|definition=Operating margin = Operating Income / Total Revenue] -->

Compared to Walmart (4.18%) and Target (4.88%), Costco’s operating margin is slightly lower, suggesting different cost structures or pricing strategies among major retailers. However, Costco’s return on average equity stood at 28.4%, calculated as net income of $9.226 billion divided by the average stockholders' equity of $32.484 billion.
<!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss|period=2025-09-01/2026-08-30|value=9226000000] -->
<!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:StockholdersEquity|period=2026-08-30|value=35803000000] -->
<!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:StockholdersEquity|period=2025-08-31|value=29164000000] -->
<!-- [source: ratio|operation=divide|inputs=9226000000;32483500000|result=28.4%|definition=Return on average equity = Net Income / ((Current Equity + Prior Equity) / 2)] -->

The price-to-earnings ratio is approximately 48.4, derived from the user-supplied price of $1,005.16 divided by diluted EPS of $20.76. This metric reflects investor expectations for future growth rather than just current performance.
<!-- [source: line|file=8-K_exhibit_99_1.txt|line=44] -->
<!-- [source: ratio|operation=divide|inputs=1005.16;20.76|result=48.42|definition=P/E = Price / Diluted EPS] -->

Free cash flow amounted to $9.382 billion, calculated as cash from operations of $15.817 billion minus capital expenditures of $6.435 billion. This indicates strong cash generation capacity that exceeds net income, supporting dividends and buybacks.
<!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities|period=2025-09-01/2026-08-30|value=15817000000] -->
<!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment|period=2025-09-01/2026-08-30|value=6435000000] -->
<!-- [source: ratio|operation=subtract|inputs=15817000000;6435000000|result=9382000000|definition=Free cash flow = Cash from Operations - CapEx] -->

Debt to equity ratio was 17.2%, computed as total debt of $6.162 billion divided by stockholders' equity of $35.803 billion. This low leverage suggests a conservative balance sheet, limiting financial risk despite ongoing capital investments.
<!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent|period=2026-08-30|value=3914000000] -->
<!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:LongTermDebtCurrent|period=2026-08-30|value=2248000000] -->
<!-- [source: xbrl|tag=us-gaap:StockholdersEquity|period=2026-08-30|value=35803000000] -->
<!-- [source: ratio|operation=divide|inputs=6162000000;35803000000|result=17.21%|definition=Debt to equity = (Long-term debt + Current debt) / Stockholders' equity] -->

Comparable sales growth for the fiscal year was 8.4% for the Total Company, with an adjusted figure of 6.6% excluding gasoline prices and foreign exchange. The Digitally-Enabled segment showed 20.9% growth, highlighting a significant digital channel contribution to overall performance.
